title.narrative: Xi'an Urban Road Network Improvement Project

description.narrative: The project impact will be to ensure the city transport system can fulfill its essential enabling role in economic development by facilitating the movements of goods and people. By contributing to a comprehensive and holistic solution for integrated urban mobility and enhanced system management, the project will promote the sustainable economic growth of the city. The project outcome will be an efficient, safe and environmentally sustainable integrated urban transport system developed in Xi'an. The project includes five interlined outputs: (i) Output 1: road network improvements; (ii) Output 2: pedestrian crossing and safety improvements; (iii) Output 3: multimodal interchange facilities; (iv) Output 4: ITS and road user safety program; (v) Output 5: environment protection enhancement.

Average bus speed along bus priority corridor increased from 14 km/h to 20 km/h and predictability of trip travel time improved Progress/Status: To be achieved. Data Source: Police accident records and statistics Actual value:
Average project corridor speeds increased to 20 km/h in 2020 (2011 baseline: 14 km/h) Progress/Status: To be achieved. Data Source: Cross-town traffic speed and commuter surveys Actual value:

Public satisfaction with pedestrian-crossing facilities (including that of such vulnerable groups as women, children, the poor, the elderly, and the disabled) increased to 75% after project completion in 2020 (2010 baseline: 20%) Progress/Status: To be achieved. Data Source: Public satisfaction survey Actual value:
Pass rate in annual vehicle emission test increased to 80% from 70% by 2020 Progress/Status: To be achieved. Data Source: Before and after household surveys for pedestrian facilities Actual value:

By 30 November 2015, 36 intersections and pedestrian crossing had been rehabilitated, including two changed from the original list. Output: 4. ITS and road user safety program Indicator: 4.1. Expansion of existing ITS infrastructure to the Third Ring Road by 2019 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Procurement of traffic video monitoring system (ITS-G01-2) and camera enforcement system (ITS-G01-3) were completed by November 2014. Procurement of dynamic traffic information collection system (ITS-G01-1) was completed and the contract was signed in September 2015. For dynamic traffic information release system (ITS-G02), the procurement was completed and contract was signed in November 2016. For road safety education equipment (ITS-G03) and high definition traffic monitoring system (ITS-G04), procurement was completed and the contracts were signed in March 2017. Data Source: ADB review missions and progress reports, and executing agency and consultant reports Project completion and acceptance records Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 4. ITS and road user safety program Indicator: 4.2. Implementation of road safety education programs by 2018, with a minimum of 50% participation of women as community facilitators or participants Achievement: Y Progress/Status: ADB approved the revised proposal, but recruitment of consulting firm encountered difficulty. No consulting firm successfully submitted EOI in CMS although the deadline was extended twice. It was agreed that XMTPD will use the domestic funds to implement this activities. The XMTPD reported to the Mission the detailed activities on road safety education conducted so far. The Mission was satisfied with the progress and requested the XMTPD to prepare a detailed report in line with the objectives and TOR of the road safety education program. The XMURCC and XMTPD proposed to use the allocated ADB finance to procure traffic safety education facilities. The Mission supported the proposal and agreed to include one equipment package (with cost estimate of $0.31 million) in the procurement plan. The Mission advised XMTPD to prepare the technical specifications and start procurement of the equipment.
